A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MP-OSPC research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic, IHDP, and ACIC experiments in Section 6 and Appendix E, plus an original COVID-19 data analysis in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds MP convergence, sensitivity, and computational-cost experiments in Appendix F. The COVID-19 analysis remains in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The main MP-OSPC estimator and its default updates remain unchanged. v2 adds a tested Gumbel-copula option for outcome-posterior updates in Appendix F.3.1, extending the Gaussian-copula implementation examined in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic generator, IHDP, 77 ACIC 2016 datasets, and COVID-19 lockdown dataset. The added diagnostics reuse existing synthetic coverage; the COVID-19 case study is relocated, not removed.

E2.justification: The concentration diagnostics expand from TabPFN MP variants in v1 to include CausalPFN at three temperatures and CausalPFN–TabPFN combinations in v2 Figure 9. Comparator membership in the matched ATE benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled protocols varying posterior draws, MP steps, copula families and their parameters, plus runtime and peak-memory measurements under specified hardware. The confounding diagnostic also switches to standardized-outcome units. Existing benchmark splits and principal ATE evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds MP convergence diagnostics, concentration checks for CausalPFN–TabPFN combinations, sensitivity to posterior draws and MP steps, Gaussian-versus-Gumbel copula tests, and computational scaling analyses. These substantially expand the evidence about numerical stability, robustness, and practical cost beyond v1's existing concentration checks.

E5.justification: IHDP Table 5 changes from mean ± standard deviation to mean ± standard error over the same 100 splits. For example, CausalPFN at T=1 changes from 0.239±0.140 to 0.239±0.014; this does not establish additional runs or reduced between-split variability.

E6.justification: v2 adds results showing ATE stability around B=75 and N=100, deteriorating CausalPFN concentration with increasing sample size, copula robustness, and lower computational costs for copula-based MPs. Reported confounding values also change with normalization, including synthetic Δ≈−3.4 becoming −0.5. Performance means in Tables 2–5 remain unchanged; these are added findings and rescaled diagnostics, not improved scores under the original settings.

T1.justification: Where v1 supports Theorem 1 through a citation, v2 Appendix A.3 supplies a proof sketch using bootstrap, empirical-process, and remainder arguments. It also qualifies replacement of the Donsker condition by sample splitting with additional convergence and envelope requirements. Appendix B.1 expands the confounding-bound derivation; Proposition 1 is retained and relocated, with a covariance-index correction.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: diagnosing prior-induced confounding bias, using OSPC to obtain conditional frequentist consistency, and implementing the correction through martingale posteriors. The principal ATE calibration and novelty claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 now distinguishes persistent bias from bias that vanishes too slowly and acknowledges that exact PFN confounding bias is intractable. Section 5.4 more explicitly attributes the dominant BvM bottleneck to the underlying PFN, while the new conclusion identifies heterogeneous-effect uncertainty as an unresolved extension. Added analyses also discuss compensation between nuisance estimators and insensitivity to copula specification.

D1.justification: v2 changes the stated code location from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. Figure 2 newly explains how prior causal datasets and TabPFN treatment assignments were obtained, and Figure 14 specifies the AMD EPYC 9455 CPU and NVIDIA H200 GPU used for profiling. Most implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Diaconis and Freedman (1986) to the consistency discussion and Fong and Yiu (2026) to the discussion of MP asymptotics. These strengthen supporting context without substantially changing the research gap or positioning; several other reference edits are publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: v2 refines wording and terminology, including changing the diagnostic label from L2-convergence to L2-concentration. It introduces a dedicated conclusion, reorganizes selected main-text discussions into a Questions & Answers appendix, and subdivides the experimental appendix. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds five multi-panel figures covering convergence, sensitivity, and computational cost. It redraws Figure 2 with normalized confounding axes and redesigns the ACIC displays with separate confounding/overlap axes and reordered datasets. The workflow diagram moves from main-text Figure 3 to appendix Figure 6, while existing tables largely retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the conditional theoretical argument more inspectable through a proof sketch and qualified sample-splitting assumptions, and adds useful evidence about numerical stability, copula sensitivity, and computational cost that v1 lacked. The bias discussion is also more precise. These improve support and clarity, while the main benchmark findings and unresolved asymptotic guarantees for current PFNs remain unchanged.
